## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Naḷamālikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 16) is a verse biographical narrative belonging to the Therīapadāna section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the past karma and spiritual achievements of an enlightened nun (therī), focusing on the spiritual merits accrued from offering a reed garland (*naḷamālā*). SuttaCentral indexes translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
Computational analysis via DharmaNexus shows widespread internal formulaic reuse within the Pali canon, registering 180 matching passages across 44 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive textual correspondence is with the commentary to the *Therīgāthā* (*Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*), which shares substantial portions of the narrative (segments 0.3–9.1 align with paragraphs 691_10–708 with 0.88 similarity), indicating the integration or quotation of this verse biography in the Therī commentary [DharmaNexus]. It also displays notable formulaic overlap with other poems in the Therīapadāna—most prominently the homonymous *Naḷamālikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 5), as well as the *Ekapiṇḍapātadāyikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 6), *Udakadāyikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 10), and *Ekūposathikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 11)—particularly in recurring stock formulas marking monastic realization and standard declarations of arahantship [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus identifies low-to-moderate cross-language formulaic alignments with Tibetan Vinaya narratives (*Vinayavastu*, D0001-2) and Kṣemendra's *Bodhisatvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155), as well as fragmentary phrase parallels in the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26), though these represent machine alignments of shared stock phrasing rather than direct translation parallels [DharmaNexus].
